PATH 200.title: Pathology and Laboratory Medicine - Myths and Misconceptions
PATH 200.description: Introduces students to pathology and laboratory medicine, addressing common misconceptions often portrayed in the media. It explores the crucial roles these disciplines play in understanding, preventing, and treating diseases.

PATH 305.title: Modern Microscopy
PATH 305.description: Theoretical and practical application of widely used microscopy techniques.

PATH 306.title: Safety for Medical Laboratory Scientists
PATH 306.description: Workplace hazards of chemical, biological and ergonomic origin.

PATH 307.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Science - Histochemistry and Hematology
PATH 307.description: Fundamentals and applications of Histochemistry. Introduction to Hematology.

PATH 308.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Science - Clinical Chemistry
PATH 308.description: Selected areas of clinical chemistry and relevant fundamentals of human physiology.

PATH 309.title: Biomolecular Foundations: Nucleic Acids, Carbohydrates and Physical Biochemistry
PATH 309.description: Basic and physical biochemical sciences relevant to medical laboratory science with application to clinical and translational research.

PATH 310.title: Biomolecular Foundations: Proteins, Lipids and Bioenergetics
PATH 310.description: Basic and physical biochemical sciences relevant to medical laboratory science with application to clinical and translational research.

PATH 311.title: Cytogenetics and Molecular Genetics
PATH 311.description: Fundamentals of human genetics and molecular techniques as they relate to detecting genetic abnormalities in research and clinical settings.

PATH 312.title: Tissue Culture and Cytology
PATH 312.description: Fundamentals as they relate to the study of cells in controlled environments and their role in cancer development within research and clinical applications.

PATH 313.title: Normal Histology – Cells and Tissues
PATH 313.description: Description and identification of human anatomy at the microscopic level and how this relates to function.

PATH 314.title: Normal Histology – Organ Systems
PATH 314.description: Description and identification of human anatomy at the microscopic level and how this relates to function.

PATH 315.title: Bacteriology, Mycology and Parasitology
PATH 315.description: Biological attributes, clinical features, pathogenesis and pathology, epidemiology, immunological reactions, laboratory diagnosis, and preventative measures of human microbial pathogens.

PATH 316.title: Virology and Public Health Fundamentals
PATH 316.description: Mechanisms of viral replication, transmission, disease progression, and laboratory diagnosis. Broader public health impact and basic strategies for prevention and control of pathogens in a larger community context.

PATH 375.title: Introduction to Human Pathology
PATH 375.description: Causes, natural history and pathophysiology of common disease processes.

children.raw: 6 credits of first year BIOL_V and 6 credits of first year CHEM_V

PATH 375.prerequisiteText: Either a) 6 credits of first year BIOL_V and 6 credits of first year CHEM_V; or b) SCIE_V 001

PATH 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
PATH 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in Winter Session of third year or Summer Session after third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students in the BMLSc Co-op Program.

PATH 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
PATH 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Coop Program in BMLSc.

PATH 405.title: Seminars in Current Topics
PATH 405.description: Oral and written presentation and critical appraisal of scientific papers.

PATH 408.title: Research and Career Skills
PATH 408.description: Overall operation of research laboratories including roles of personnel and funding; communication of scientific research; career skills and pathways; communication, collaboration, presentations and peer-assessment skills.

PATH 409.title: Advanced Hematology
PATH 409.description: Theoretical and practical examination of modern concepts which relate to the practice of medical laboratory science.

PATH 410.title: Hematological Malignancies
PATH 410.description: A comprehensive overview that includes pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and treatment.

PATH 411.title: Diagnostic Histochemistry
PATH 411.description: Theoretical and practical application of histochemical techniques.

PATH 412.title: Introduction to Advanced Techniques in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
PATH 412.description: Theoretical foundations and practical applications of advanced pathology and laboratory medicine techniques in both research and clinical settings.

PATH 413.title: Analytical Techniques and Basic Tests in Clinical Chemistry
PATH 413.description: Biochemistry tests in clinical medicine and the analytical chemistry techniques used to produce the results; pathophysiology of common clinical conditions.

PATH 414.title: Specialized Tests in Clinical Chemistry
PATH 414.description: Biochemistry tests in clinical medicine; pathophysiology of common clinical conditions.

PATH 415.title: Immunopathology
PATH 415.description: Innate and adaptive immunity and how these host defense mechanisms are involved in both health and illness.

PATH 416.title: Clinical Toxicology
PATH 416.description: A theoretical and practical examination of analytical and pathophysiological aspects related to detection and management in medical laboratories.

PATH 417.title: Human Infections
PATH 417.description: Physiologic alterations, virulence factors, clinical microbiology, treatments, and applied epidemiology through self-directed learning and small group case-based discussions.
notes: 3 credits of second year MICB_V (MICB_V 212 recommended).

PATH 418.title: Forensic Toxicology and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
PATH 418.description: A theoretical and practical examination of analytical and pathophysiological aspects related to detection and management in medical laboratories.

PATH 427.title: Basic Principles of Infection Prevention and Control
PATH 427.description: This course provides the basic principles to prevent the spread of microorganisms pathogenic to humans. It may be taken towards a Certificate in Infection Control.

PATH 437.title: Viral Infections in Humans
PATH 437.description: Interactions between viruses and humans; pathogenesis; prompt virological diagnosis; rationale for antiviral chemotherapy and prophylaxis.

PATH 438.title: Medical Laboratory Science: Directed Studies
PATH 438.description: Investigation of a specific topic in Medical Laboratory Science.

PATH 447.title: Directed Studies
PATH 447.description: An elective in clinical infection control, medical microbiology or molecular biology.

PATH 448.title: Introduction to Laboratory Medicine
PATH 448.description: An elective course open to first-year medical students who spend at least three consecutive hours each week in one of the affiliated hospitals of the Department of Pathology, Vancouver Hospital, under the joint supervision of a Senior Resident in Pathology and the Professional Staff of the following Divisions: anatomical pathology, clinical biochemistry, hematology, pediatric pathology. Enrolment is limited.

PATH 450.title: Systemic Pathology
PATH 450.description: A series of Pathology discussions in conjunction with various clinical departments designed to illustrate the role of Pathology in the diagnosis and management of various diseases.

PATH 451.title: Clerkship in Laboratory Medicine and Infection Prevention and Control
PATH 451.description: May involve attendance at an approved institution and/or a project assigned by the instructor(s). Instructor permission required. Enrolment may be limited.

PATH 452.title: Clerkship in Anatomic Pathology
PATH 452.description: An elective course open to third-year medical students, designed to familiarize the student with Anatomic Pathology, including Surgical Pathology, Pediatric Pathology, Autopsy Pathology and Cytology. This elective may involve attendance at one or more affiliated hospitals. Registration requires consent of the Department and enrolment may be limited.

PATH 453.title: Clinical Laboratory Hematology
PATH 453.description: Correlative seminars based on haematology case studies relating clinical features to laboratory investigations.

PATH 457.title: Clinical Laboratory Microbiology
PATH 457.description: Selected clinical laboratory exercises plus seminars to illustrate the diagnosis and management of patients with microbial infections. Elective course limited to third- and fourth-year medical students.

PATH 467.title: Basic Microbiology for Infection Control
PATH 467.description: The identification, clinical significance, and transmission of pathogenic organisms are presented. This course is available by correspondence or webCT. It may be taken towards fulfillment of the Certificate in Infection Control.

PATH 477.title: Basic Epidemiology for Infection Control
PATH 477.description: Epidemiology, study, design and analysis, and outbreak investigation as it applies to institutional infection control.

PATH 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
PATH 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Coop Program in BMLSc.

PATH 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
PATH 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Coop Program in BMLSc.

PATH 501.title: Foundations of Human Histopathology
PATH 501.description: Microscopic anatomy of human tissues and organs in health and disease. Principles of histological analysis and applications in pathology.

PATH 502.title: Current Topics in Pathology Research
PATH 502.description: General principles of etiology, pathogenesis, disordered physiology, and anatomic pathology of common disease processes.

PATH 518.title: Pulmonary Pathophysiology
PATH 518.description: A review of current topics in pulmonary pathophysiology at an advanced level suitable for graduate students majoring in pathology, medicine, surgery or anesthesiology. Topics will include lung anatomy, ventilation, blood flow, gas and fluid exchange.

PATH 521.title: Introduction to the Pathogenesis of Human Disease
PATH 521.description: Current medical research; cardiovascular and pulmonary disease.

PATH 523.title: Principles of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy
PATH 523.description: Classification, structure and mode of action of antimicrobial agents. In-depth comparison of factors affecting the activity of antimicrobials in vivo and in vitro.

PATH 527.title: Bacteriology, Mycology, Virology and Parasitology
PATH 527.description: All groups of microorganisms pathogenic for humans. Clinical features, pathogenesis and pathology, epidemiology, properties of the agents, immunology, laboratory diagnosis, therapy, preventative measures.

PATH 530.title: Nutrition and Metabolic Aspects of Human Disease
PATH 530.description: Molecular effects of changes in nutrient status and metabolism on health.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students registered in the Pathology Graduate Program or instructor approval required

PATH 530.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students registered in the Pathology Graduate Program or instructor approval required

PATH 531.title: Molecular and Cell Biology of Cancer
PATH 531.description: Focuses on molecular and cell biology of cancer through a series of lectures, reviews, student presentations and discussion. Recommended prerequisites: One of BIOL_V 234, BIOL_V 335, BIOC_V 303, MEDG_V 421. Course coordinator permission is required.

PATH 535.title: Seminar
PATH 535.description: Attendance required of all M.Sc. candidates in the Department.

PATH 547.title: Techniques in Molecular Biology and Experimental Pathology
PATH 547.description: Nucleic acid purification and characterization; restriction enzyme digests; northern and southern blotting; cloning; DNA sequencing; polymerase chain reaction technology; electron microscopy; fluorescein-activated cell sorting. .

PATH 570.title: Cardiovascular Pathophysiology
PATH 570.description: Pathogenesis, abnormal physiology, and therapeutic approaches in heart disease including cardiac arrhythmia, heart failure, myocardial infarction, hypertension, atherosclerosis.

PATH 582.title: Toxicology III: Environmental Toxicology
PATH 582.description: Toxicology and risk assessment of air, water and soil pollutants; food additives; animal and plant toxins; pesticides; heavy metals; solvents. .

PATH 583.title: Toxicology IV: Molecular Mechanisms of Toxicology
PATH 583.description: Activation versus detoxification by cytochromes P-450; the role of the Ah receptor; reactive oxygen species; heavy metals; apoptosis. .

PATH 635.title: Seminar
PATH 635.description: Attendance required for all Ph.D. candidates in the department.

PATH 700.title: Pathology Conference
PATH 700.description: Review and analysis of current cases. Diagnostic and pathogenic significance of findings are assessed. One hour weekly.

PATH 701.title: Surgical Pathology
PATH 701.description: Five days per week, one-hour review of current diagnostic biopsy problems. Diagnostic and therapeutic implications are discussed.

PATH 702.title: Hematologic Pathology
PATH 702.description: Lectures and seminars on the pathology of hematological diseases. Two hours weekly.

PATH 703.title: Histochemical Pathology
PATH 703.description: A series of lectures and seminars to show current applications of histochemical techniques to contemporary pathological diagnosis. One hour weekly per quarter.

PATH 704.title: Hematologic Pathology
PATH 704.description: Analysis of pathology of bone marrow aspirates; taken in one half or whole year. One and one-half hours weekly. Pass/Fail.

PATH 705.title: Clinical Chemistry
PATH 705.description: A series of lectures, seminars, tutorials, and laboratory tuition to demonstrate the use of chemical analysis in clinical medicine. Two hours weekly.

PATH 706.title: Neuropathology
PATH 706.description: Sectioning of necropsy material with clinicopathological correlation. One hour weekly.

PATH 707.title: Neuropathology, Clinical Correlation
PATH 707.description: Pathology of central nervous system disease demonstrated to clinical staff, stressing correlation with clinical diseases. Two hours weekly.

PATH 708.title: Dermatopathology
PATH 708.description: Clinicopathological correlation of dermal lesions. Discussion of pathogenesis, clinical course, and prognostic implications. One hour weekly.

PATH 709.title: Renal Biopsy Rounds
PATH 709.description: Weekly correlation between clinical status and pathological findings in several patients.

PATH 710.title: Hepatic and Gastrointestinal Pathology
PATH 710.description: Clinicopathologial correlation of hepatic and gastrointestinal biopsy material with discussions of pathogenesis, etiology, and therapeutic implications. Alternate weeks, one hour.

PATH 711.title: Cytology
PATH 711.description: Daily review of cytopathology. Analysis of cervical and sputum smears and pleural, gastric, and bronchial aspirates with discussion of significance to patients, taken in one quater of year.

PATH 712.title: Perinatal Mortality Conference
PATH 712.description: Discussion of perinatal mortality cases for the month, with review of clinical and laboratory findings, management, and pathology findings by pediatric, obstetrical, and pathology teaching staff. Methods of possible prevention of fetal or neonatal death are discussed and recommended as hypothetical reasons for preventability, where appropriate. Two hours monthly. Pass/Fail.

PATH 713.title: Seminars in Biochemical Pediatrics
PATH 713.description: A series of discussions on clinical problems which are chosen to illustrate the biochemical basis for the practice of pediatrics.

PATH 714.title: Pediatric Pathology
PATH 714.description: Demonstration and dissection of congenital heart lesions; correlation of cardiological and pathological data. One hour weekly.

PATH 720.title: Microbiological Diagnosis
PATH 720.description: Conduct of bacterial, fungal, parasitological, and viral laboratory tests relevant to the microbiological examination of patients. For medical residents.

PATH 721.title: Microbiological Research
PATH 721.description: Conduct of research on some aspect of clinical or basic microbiology. For medical residents.

PATH 722.title: Microbial Infections
PATH 722.description: Review in depth of syndromes caused by common human pathogenic bacteria, fungi and viruses, including principles of current laboratory diagnostic procedures and the rational use of antibiotics and prophylactic agents. For medical residents.

PATH 725.title: Histopathology of Infectious Diseases
PATH 725.description: Gross and microscopic changes associated with infections, and the pathophysiology involved in their development. The course includes seminars based on histological specimens. For residents in Medical Microbiology, General and Anatomical Pathology, and Infectious Diseases.
